detailed_findings.finding: Genus-0 case is fully justified: genus 0 forces no missing nonnegative integers, hence S = N_0, and conversely N_0 is a numerical semigroup of genus 0.

Genus-1 classification is correct: if the unique missing element m were >= 2, then 1 in S and closure under addition would force all n >= 0 into S, contradicting m notin S; hence m = 1, and the converse verification of the explicit set is complete.

Genus-2 classification is correct: 1 cannot lie in S, so the missing set is {1,m}; if m >= 4 then both 2 and m-2 lie in S, forcing m in S by closure, contradiction; thus m is 2 or 3, yielding exactly the two listed semigroups.
Both candidate genus-2 sets are explicitly checked to be cofinite additive submonoids containing 0, so the existence direction is complete.
The conclusion N(0)=1, N(1)=1, N(2)=2 and hence N(2)=N(1)+N(0) matches the lemma statement and the intended boundary-case role for g = 2.

reason: The proof correctly classifies numerical semigroups of genus 0, 1, and 2 using only the definition of numerical semigroup and genus. Each uniqueness direction and each existence check is supplied, and the final count N(0)=1, N(1)=1, N(2)=2 implies the required boundary-case inequality N(2) >= N(1)+N(0). There is no substantive semantic drift from the lemma sketch or its role in the assembly, and no undeclared or forbidden dependencies are used.
